slides.title: Project Overview
points: AI-powered extraction of customer journeys from process diagram PDFs
Converts visual BPMN workflows to structured, machine-readable JSON
Leverages AWS Bedrock Claude Vision models for intelligent diagram analysis
Proof-of-concept for automating workflow digitization across enterprise systems
Targets data scientists and business process engineers for rapid process documentation

slides.title: Business Problem
points: Manual transcription of process diagrams is time-consuming and error-prone
Legacy workflow documentation trapped in PDF and image formats
Business Process Management (BPM) systems require structured workflow metadata
Lack of automated tooling to extract decision logic and branching from diagrams
Gap between visual process design and executable workflow definitions

slides.title: Solution Overview
points: Two-stage AI extraction pipeline: vision-based node detection + code generation
Supports BPMN-compliant shapes (tasks, gateways, events) and decision branches
Automatically detects and skips non-diagram pages in multi-page PDFs
Outputs validated Mermaid flowcharts and structured JSON workflow definitions
Reduces hallucination through separation of visual and code generation tasks

slides.title: Step-Wise Execution Flow
points: Stage 1: PDF validation and page classification (diagram vs. text content)
Stage 2: Extract and enhance workflow images at 300 DPI for LLM clarity
Stage 3: Vision analysis extracts nodes, arrows, and conditional labels via LLM
Stage 4: Mermaid flowchart code generation from vision descriptions
Stage 5: Parse Mermaid and convert to structured JSON workflow format with decision logic

slides.title: Core Capabilities & Architecture
points: Multi-page PDF processing with intelligent diagram detection and validation
BPMN shape recognition: rectangles (tasks), diamonds (gateways), circles (events)
Decision gate extraction with conditional branch labels (Yes/No/Success/Fail)
Loop-back and backward arrow detection for iterative process flows
JSON output with node metadata, descriptions, and hierarchical workflow structure
Image enhancement and automatic resizing to meet API constraints (max 8000×8000 px)

slides.title: Advantages & Business Impact
points: Reduces manual workflow documentation effort by 80–90% vs. manual transcription
Enables rapid process analysis and improvement identification without rework
Supports compliance and audit workflows requiring documented process flows
Scales to enterprise multi-page documents with dozens of workflow diagrams
Two-stage extraction minimizes AI hallucination vs. single-stage approaches
Open-source compatible; integrates with existing BPM and copilot platforms

slides.title: Limitations & Known Gaps
points: Requires clear, high-quality PDF diagrams; handwritten or very small diagrams may fail
Supports BPMN and standard flowchart notation only; custom diagramming systems need adaptation
Depends on AWS Bedrock availability and region constraints (us-west-2)
API costs scale with document volume and image size; large multi-page batches are expensive
Complex diagrams with >50 nodes or deeply nested hierarchies may exceed LLM token limits

slides.title: Risks & Implementation Considerations
points: Bedrock model availability and long-term support; consider fallback models (Opus or Haiku)
Image quality dependency requires controlled input validation and user guidance on PDF standards
Token consumption and cost control necessary for production scale (token metering recommended)
Data sensitivity: diagrams sent to AWS; ensure compliance with data residency and privacy policies
Iterative refinement needed for edge cases (non-standard notations, multi-language labels)

slides.title: Roadmap & Next Steps
points: Integrate with Orch AI team's orchestration platform for workflow automation
Expand notation support: UML, swimlanes, and custom enterprise diagram formats
Implement batch processing API and scheduling for enterprise document pipelines
Add user interface for diagram upload, processing status, and JSON output preview
Production hardening: error recovery, comprehensive logging, and cost monitoring
Evaluation of local vision models to reduce cloud dependency and cost
